title: Runtime Persistence Write Authority - Governed Response Chunks

phases.objective: Bind the governed response chunk lifecycle to an explicit DB_USER runtime-persistence privilege contract while preserving owner isolation, integrity, no-secret policy, TTL, schema readiness, and bounded cleanup, and inventory every direct getPool()/db.js SQL mutation surface for follow-up classification.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Governed response chunk persist/load/expiry lifecycle using db.js DB_USER
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The runtime fails closed before unauthorized DB mutation, preserves cross-owner isolation and response integrity, performs bounded expiry cleanup only with DELETE authority, and exposes a complete classified source inventory for the remaining direct DB mutation surfaces.
steps: Resolve the ordinary runtime database identity through the existing DB_USER-backed getPool() path.
Read bounded MariaDB privilege metadata without exposing credential or account values.
Require direct table privileges for the requested governed_tool_response_chunks operation and reject broad write authority paths.
Persist only non-secret owned chunks and verify the stored SHA-256 before acknowledging persistence.
Reject cross-tenant and cross-workspace reads and overwrite attempts without mutating the stored response.
Require UPDATE authority before sliding TTL extension and DELETE authority before bounded expired-row cleanup.
Reconstruct a durable Arabic/emoji response after memory-cache eviction and verify hash, byte length, cursor policy, and TTL extension.
Scan all direct getPool()/db.js SQL mutation surfaces and classify each as ordinary runtime persistence, governance/control-plane, or migration/DDL/admin.
Do not modify platformResourceAuthorityGrantTool.js or Governance Migration lifecycle and do not execute live Production SQL, grants, or secret writes.
assertions: DB_USER remains the shared ordinary runtime writer; no separate one-table Runtime Persistence Writer credential is introduced.
governed_tool_response_chunks requires direct SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE across its complete lifecycle.
Persist fails before mutation when SELECT, INSERT, or UPDATE authority required by the hot path is missing.
Expiry cleanup fails before DELETE when DELETE authority is missing.
Global/schema write privileges, extra target-table privileges, column grants, grant option, and applicable roles fail the bounded target-table authority proof.
Unrelated direct table privileges do not fail this table-specific proof because DB_USER is a shared runtime writer.
Unauthorized principals cannot read or overwrite another owner's chunk and same-owner overwrite remains allowed.
SHA-256, UTF-8 byte length, secret rejection, positive TTL, expiry rejection, and schema readiness remain enforced.
The inventory emits only the three approved classification values and keeps Window 2's platformResourceAuthorityGrantTool.js visible without modifying it.
No migration, Production SQL, GRANT, database-user, deployment, or secret mutation is performed by this source PR.

phases.objective: Prove the exact Production DB_USER target-table privilege state after this source is promoted without exposing database credentials.
blockers: The source repair must first pass PR CI/E2E and the normal main-to-Production promotion lifecycle.
Production DB_USER direct grants for governed_tool_response_chunks have not been read back through this source contract.
Any required Production privilege adjustment must use separately governed database administrative authority outside this PR.

phases.objective: Extend bounded runtime-persistence privilege contracts to additional ordinary write lifecycles selected from the canonical inventory without mixing governance or migration authority.
This source slice adds no external provider write canary; durable chunk integration is covered synthetically and Production DB changes are separately governed.
Treat runtime persistence authority as Production-ready only after exact source promotion and a bounded DB_USER privilege readback proves the table contract.
blockers: No live Production privilege evidence is produced by this source PR.
No Production SQL or grant mutation is authorized by this phase.
